question: Should OpenClaw adopt this exact versioned recovery-point composition contract in core before the RFC assigns ownership of inventory selection, recovery obligations, and the host lifecycle boundary?
rationale: The patch is not merely an internal refactor: its deterministic IDs and quarantine rules are consumed by stacked capture and restore work, so landing it selects a persistent product and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Adopt the proposed core seam
options.body: Approve the private composer as the initial core recovery contract while retaining ingress, storage, wake, placement, and compute lifecycle in the host.

options.title: Define a narrower RFC seam first
options.body: Pause the stack until maintainers specify a different inventory, obligation, or ownership boundary, then adapt the implementation to that decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt the proposed core seam
recommendation.body: Approve the private composer as the initial core recovery contract while retaining ingress, storage, wake, placement, and compute lifecycle in the host.
